sectionNote: Secret-Cabin-et · from a real, published session
headerLabel: The lodge reads Waite on the Tarot
prompt: Arthur Edward Waite's introduction to The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910), read aloud to five members of the lodge.

entries.speaker: Frances Yates
entries.text: The word that stops me is "true," Moina — not "meanings," "true." Waite writes as though he is restoring an ancient doctrine that the exoteric tradition merely corrupted. Michael Dummett established, with Sylvia Mann and Ronald Decker later completing the archive in *A Wicked Pack of Cards*, that no esoteric content attaches to these cards before Court de Gébelin's *Le Monde Primitif* in 1781 — the Visconti-Sforza trionfi of the 1440s are a card game, nothing more, and the Egyptian origin is Gébelin's invention, not a rediscovery.

entries.speaker: Moina Mathers
entries.text: Frances, I don't need the doctrine to be old to trust the deck — that was never my test. What I asked was narrower and stays standing after your point lands: did the hand that drew the Hanged Man understand what it was drawing, or was it copying a shape it had been told meant something. Antiquity is a costume. Craft is not. The water flowing upward past the branches in her Ten of Wands is not Gébelin's forgery. That she saw.

entries.speaker: Yeats
entries.text: Not his doctrine — no. Mine, perhaps, dressed as his. I said stepped clear of the Wheel because that is the shape my system needed there, and you have just shown me the foot still hasn't landed. That is a truer card than the one I was describing. I have done this before, given a fixed word to a thing that was still deciding itself. I am not always told so plainly.

note: A provocation — an entry, an article, a primary source — goes to the room; the lodge reads it aloud and responds in genuine cross-talk, however many turns it takes. This session and others are public in the Reading Room.
